Edge functions should use the connection pooler on port **6543** (transaction mode) instead of the direct connection on port 5432. The pooler is designed for serverless and edge workloads that open many short-lived connections and helps avoid "too many connections" errors. You can find the pooler connection string in your project's Database settings, where you can also adjust the pool size per client if needed. [product/connection-pooling.md]

Point your serverless functions at the connection pooler on port 6543 (transaction mode) instead of the direct connection on port 5432, and lower the pool size per client. You can adjust the pool size in Database settings. [product/connection-pooling.md]
The pool size per client for the connection pooler is set in **Database settings** in your project dashboard. From the docs: "Pool size is set in Database settings." [product/connection-pooling.md]
On a paid plan, daily backups are kept for 7 days [product/backups.md].

Point-in-time recovery is an add-on, not included with the standard daily backups on paid plans. Paid plans keep daily backups for 7 days, and point-in-time recovery is available as a separate add-on [product/backups.md].

Yes. According to the backups documentation, restoring a backup replaces the whole database and takes the project offline during the restore. If you need to keep newer data, download a logical backup first. [product/backups.md]

I understand you need to recover data from yesterday's backup. According to our documentation, restoring a backup replaces the entire database and takes the project offline during the restore [product/backups.md]. 

Since you mentioned only specific rows were deleted, you may want to consider downloading a logical backup first to extract just the data you need, rather than doing a full restore that would overwrite any newer data.

A support engineer will follow up to assist you with the backup restoration process if that's what you'd like to proceed with.
